hints: Look closely at the carbon attached to the halogen in 1-chlorobutane and 1-iodobutane and decide whether it is primary, secondary or tertiary.
Both molecules are primary halogenoalkanes, so think about whether a primary carbocation could form easily or whether direct attack by $\text{OH}^-$ is preferred.
Compare the $\text{C-Cl}$ and $\text{C-I}$ bond strengths to work out which bond breaks more easily and so gives the faster substitution.
walkthrough:
**Identify the type of halogenoalkane**

Both 1-chlorobutane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, and 1-iodobutane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}$, have the halogen on the end carbon.

That carbon is attached to only one other carbon, so both are primary halogenoalkanes.

**Choose SN1 or SN2**

Remember the two pathways for nucleophilic substitution with $\text{OH}^-$:
$$\text{R-X} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-OH} + \text{X}^-$$
SN1 needs a stable carbocation intermediate, which primary carbocations are not. SN2 is one direct attack by $\text{OH}^-$, which suits unhindered primary molecules perfectly.

**Compare the rate, C-Cl versus C-I**

The rate-determining factor here is how easily the $\text{C-X}$ bond breaks. The $\text{C-I}$ bond is longer and weaker than the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond, so $\text{I}^-$ is a much better leaving group than $\text{Cl}^-$.

Therefore 1-iodobutane reacts faster by the SN2 mechanism.

options.A: Incorrect. 1-chlorobutane is slower because C-Cl is stronger than C-I, and a primary halogenoalkane does not follow SN1 because a primary carbocation is too unstable to form.
options.B: Half right but wrong rate. SN2 is correct for a primary halogenoalkane, but 1-chlorobutane is slower than 1-iodobutane because Cl- is a poorer leaving group than I-.
options.C: Half right but wrong mechanism. 1-iodobutane is indeed faster, but SN1 is wrong. Primary molecules do not ionise to form a primary carbocation, they react by direct SN2 attack.
options.D: Correct. Both are primary so SN2 is followed, and 1-iodobutane is fastest because the weak C-I bond breaks most easily, making iodide the best leaving group.
